page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head at the top and the page number at the top right. The catchword and gathering signature sit at the foot.

main_text.p: liani[?] obiecerint apoplexiam, paralysin & epilepsiam, in quibus effectibus praeter na-turam laeditur sentiendi mouendiq; facultas: quoniam laeso cerebro, functiones eius laedi ac impediri necesse est. Laeduntur au-te cerebri actiones, vel temperamento eius mutato vel dissolutione continui, vel deniq; mala coformatione. Sunt enim hi affectus prauarum omnium actionum nostri corpo-ris causae proximae: non autem spiritus animalis laesus. Adde quod in plexu retiformi nullum spiritum gigni posse, duas ob cau-sas ostedimus. Primum eo plexu, aut similí cor nō utitur ad vitalis procreationem,sed ipsum e sanguine defecato in suis finibus producit.Deinde in venis & arteriis,quod partes neruosae sint,& consequenter frigi-dae,is formari nequit. Quod utiq; medico-rum nullus negare potest. At plexus retiformis plurimis constat arteriis. Igitur in eo nullus fit animalis spiritus,sed spiritum vi-talem,quo cerebrum utitur ad sua munia fun-genda,continet. Quare si quispiam denuo generatur spiritus in cerebro, is fane in fi-nibus eius potius,quam in arteriis, aut ve-nis procreari probabilius est. At vero in ce-rebri ventriculis natura frigidis nullus spi-ritus

page.notes: The first word of the page, "liani", is cut off at the top of the line and I could not read it with certainty. "similí" carries an accent-like mark I read as í; the printer's mark may differ. Printed spelling is kept throughout (e.g. "fane", "coformatione", "producit.Deinde" without a space, "sint,&"). Long s is written as plain s, so "oftedimus" becomes "ostedimus" and "poteft" becomes "potest". The running head and page number are transcribed as printed, with capital U written as U in "CAUSAS". No marginal notes are visible.
